items.title: Add an English glossary and CLI style guide to the plan document
items.context: Add a glossary + style-guide section near the top of the plan doc. Glossary fixes term choice: blocked (execution deny) vs excluded (scope) vs avoid 'forbidden'; 'source of truth' not 'truth source'; 'iteration' not 'round' in review loops; Story (product object) vs story; evidence as uncountable; Git (product) vs git (command); 'finding' not 'finding item'; 'real-machine tests' KEPT (code term realMachineTests). Style guide: command descriptions = imperative verb + sentence case + no final period; boolean flags = Enable/Disable/Emit/Skip/Fail if; schema fields = noun phrases; preserve command names, enum values, JSON keys, IDs, filenames, legacy aliases. Covers suggestions #1, #15, #20.

grep for style guide heading in plan doc finds exactly one CLI Style Guide section containing rules for imperative verb, sentence case, no final period, boolean flag patterns (Enable/Disable/Emit/Skip/Fail if), schema noun phrases, and preserve-identifiers rule; WHY: confirms style guide section was added with all required formatting rules
glossary section appears before the first M-row (M001) in the document confirming near-top placement; WHY: placement requirement from context

items.title: Apply the glossary and style across all 762 manifest rows and the T-table
items.context: Sweep M001..M762 and the T-table catalog, keeping T/M twins consistent (the F-005 lesson). items.title: Shorten over-long command descriptions, moving rules to schema/longHelp
items.context: 117 command-description rows; longest 218 chars, median 70. CLI help lists need short imperative summaries; detailed rules belong in longHelp/schema descriptions. Shorten at least M215 (artifact_declare), M339 (DONE summary), M543 (INIT reviewer fallback attestation), M650 (dev-memory finish), M655 (session-start wrapper). Covers suggestion #2.

happy.desc: measure character length of proposedEnglish for every command-description row -> none exceeds 80 characters (or a stated threshold); the previously-longest row (218 chars) is now under the limit; WHY: the core deliverable is shortening over-long descriptions

specifically check M215/M339/M543/M650/M655 proposedEnglish are shortened to imperative verb + sentence case + no final period format; WHY: these 5 rows are explicitly named in context as must-shorten
the shortened rows still convey the original command purpose (not just truncated mid-sentence); each begins with an imperative verb; WHY: shortening must not destroy meaning

edge.desc: rows at exactly the length threshold (e.g. 79 or 80 chars) are left alone and not over-shortened to trivial stubs; WHY: boundary condition -- only over-long rows should be shortened
the detailed rules removed from command descriptions appear in a schema/longHelp note or annotation (not simply deleted); WHY: context says rules move to schema/longHelp, not disappear

command-description rows that were already short (median 70 chars) are unchanged by CHK-003; diff shows no edits to rows under threshold; WHY: over-zealous shortening of already-good rows is scope creep

items.title: Isolate behavior-sensitive rows and require test updates
items.context: Some rows are runtime code, not prose: M668/M669 (cli-engine.ts:2303/2306) are regexes matching Chinese strings via .test(combined); translating away the Chinese branches changes runtime matching. Tag such rows 'behavior-sensitive; requires test update', document the risk, and do NOT treat them as ordinary translation. Identify the full set (regex / .test / .match / parsing over Chinese tokens). Covers suggestion #4.

happy.desc: M668 and M669 are tagged with behavior-sensitive; requires test update marker in their proposedEnglish or a dedicated annotation column; WHY: these two rows are the known behavior-sensitive cases from context

a Behavior-sensitive rows subsection exists in the plan document listing all identified rows with their cli-engine.ts line references and the reason (regex/.test/.match over Chinese); WHY: context requires documenting the risk not just tagging

grep cli-engine.ts for all regex/.test/.match patterns that reference Chinese string literals -> every such occurrence has a corresponding M-row tagged behavior-sensitive; WHY: the full set must be identified not just M668/M669

edge.desc: rows that use .test() or .match() but only on English strings or identifiers (not Chinese) are NOT tagged behavior-sensitive -> false positives excluded; WHY: over-tagging dilutes the signal
if additional behavior-sensitive rows beyond M668/M669 are found, they are all listed with line references and rationale; WHY: context says identify the full set, partial enumeration is a defect

behavior-sensitive rows are explicitly excluded from the CHK-002 glossary sweep (their proposedEnglish is not treated as ordinary prose translation); WHY: the plan execution order puts CHK-004 before CHK-002 precisely for this reason

adversarial.desc: attempt to apply the glossary sweep to a behavior-sensitive row (e.g. change a Chinese regex pattern in M668 proposedEnglish) -> the tag prevents this and the row retains its original code-aware translation; WHY: adversarial scenario where a bulk find-replace silently corrupts runtime code

the behavior-sensitive tag uses the exact string from the context (behavior-sensitive; requires test update) not a paraphrase -> grep-checkable marker; WHY: downstream automation or reviewers may grep for this exact string
762-row count and zero-Chinese-in-proposedEnglish invariants still hold after CHK-004 (behavior-sensitive rows are tagged but not deleted or merged); WHY: tagging must not break structural invariants

items.title: Define and apply a wrapped-source merge rule for multi-line source
items.context: Line-level splitting breaks one logical sentence across rows, producing fragments that read wrong alone (M004/M005 are one Chinese sentence about runCli({extraTools, extraRegister}) merging utils tools and handlers). Add a documented rule that a wrapped multi-line source is reviewed/translated as one unit, and apply it to M004/M005 and similar pairs. Covers suggestion #3.

happy.desc: a documented Wrapped-source merge rule section exists in the plan document explaining that multi-line source fragments forming one logical sentence are reviewed and translated as one unit; WHY: the rule must be documented not just applied

M004 and M005 are annotated as a merged pair (e.g. via a merge-group marker or cross-reference) and their combined proposedEnglish reads as one coherent sentence about runCli extraTools/extraRegister; WHY: M004/M005 are the canonical example from context
any other fragmented pairs similar to M004/M005 are also identified and annotated with the merge rule; WHY: context says apply to M004/M005 and similar pairs

edge.desc: M004 and M005 remain as two separate rows (not collapsed into one) preserving the 762-row invariant -> the merge rule is a translation/review annotation not a row deletion; WHY: merging rows would break the 762<->762 invariant

the merge rule clearly defines criteria for identifying wrapped-source pairs (e.g. a sentence split across adjacent rows where neither fragment is grammatically complete alone) -> the rule is reproducible not ad-hoc; WHY: vague rules cannot be applied consistently

if no additional fragmented pairs beyond M004/M005 exist, the document explicitly states M004/M005 is the only identified case -> absence of others is documented not silent; WHY: a reviewer cannot distinguish found-none from did-not-look

adversarial.desc: verify M004 proposedEnglish alone is marked as incomplete/partial (not a standalone translation) -> if someone reads M004 without M005 they see the merge annotation; WHY: adversarial scenario where a row-by-row implementer processes M004 in isolation
762-row count still exactly 762 after CHK-005 -> merge annotations did not accidentally add or remove rows; WHY: structural invariant must survive all checklist items

the merge rule does not conflict with the behavior-sensitive tagging from CHK-004 (if a behavior-sensitive row is also part of a wrapped pair, both annotations coexist); WHY: adversarial cross-item interaction -- two annotation systems must not clobber each other
